audit.why: TRICKY 7/10 fits: Lux owns levels 1-5 against a melee mage with no dash, and Kassadin owns everything from first item onward once Riftwalk is 5s/3.5s/2s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[0..4].side read 'Skill' while content win[0..4] and the packet both read 'Lux'. Worse, phases[5].why and phases[6].why described Lux winning those stages while the side already said Kassadin.
audit.why: The lane's shape is not even early: Kassadin has no mobility until 6 and Null Sphere's shield is delayed, so Lux zones him off farm. From first item Riftwalk flips it.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side -> Lux with all five whys rewritten, and phases[5..6].why rewritten to argue Kassadin's side as their rows already state.

audit.whatIsWrong: Void Stone (reduced magic damage, ignores unit collision) was never mentioned anywhere on the page, and Nether Blade's auto-attack reset was not flagged as the burst tell. The cooldown field claimed a 'fifteen-second invitation' on an ability that is 5/3.5/2 seconds.
audit.why: Riot's text: passive 'takes reduced magic damage and ignores unit collision'; W active is a bonus-damage next attack (7s); R 'Multiple Riftwalks in a short period of time cost additional Mana'.
audit.corrected: Void Stone's magic reduction now sits in the Don'ts, the Nether Blade wind-up is named as the step-back cue, and the cooldown field carries Riftwalk 5s/3.5s/2s, Force Pulse 21s-17s and Null Sphere 9s-7s.

audit.why: Force Pulse charges from spells cast in his vicinity, so Lux's own poke arms his slow — this is now stated in the cooldown field rather than left implicit.

edits.before: Bully the melee mage all lane — but every spell you cast feeds his shield; poke with E placement and autos, save Q for the post-shield window.
edits.after: Bully the melee mage all lane — but every spell near him charges Force Pulse and Void Stone eats magic damage; poke with E placement and autos.

edits.after: Kassadin wins by reaching 6 with farm intact, blinking 500 at a time through your skillshots, and bursting you before a second spell lands.

edits.before: Final Spark online — anything the root catches dies to the laser math. The lane becomes a geometry quiz.
edits.after: Final Spark online, and so is Riftwalk — ahead, Q into E-R still deletes him before his blinks ramp.

edits.before: Luden's spike: Q-E-R deletes squishies from root range. Force him to dodge or die on every contact.
edits.after: First item plus R: he blinks in, silences, and burns through your shield. Hold Q purely as self-peel.

edits.before: Late Lux decides fights from a screen away: root the entry, slow the pit, and laser the clump your team froze.
edits.after: His Riftwalk resets and scaling out-carry you: sit deepest, laser from 3340, and never be his closest target.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. It governs your forward steps. - W Prismatic Barrier spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Riftwalk: 5s at rank 1, 3.5s at 2, 2s at 3 — it never really goes down, so stop waiting for it. - Force Pulse: 21s to 17s, and your spells cast near him charge it. - Null Sphere: 9s to 7s. - Your Q is 10s: keep it for his blink-in.

edits.before: Carry through the root-laser pipeline — one binding per fight, converted at screen range; your job is owning the geometry that makes it land.
edits.after: Carry by ending it before Riftwalk stacks — root his walk-up, laser his recall path, and take every plate his immobile early game hands you.

edits.before: If Kassadin opens the score, reset expectations and respect Riftwalk doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with E clears and stay relevant through root picks.
edits.after: If Kassadin opens the score he reaches his item spike early — deny waves under tower with E and stop dueling him. After a second, farm with E clears and stay relevant through root picks.

edits.before: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and 2s at rank 3 — never truly down, so Q answers his arrival, not his approach.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: Riftwalk covers 500 per blink — a centered wave and warded flanks make him spend two of them, and each repeat costs him extra mana.

edits.before: Kassadin burns Riftwalk on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Kassadin burns mana on repeat Riftwalks — that stacked cost is your window.

edits.before: That’s Kassadin’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Void Stone already cuts your magic damage, and Null Sphere shields the rest.

edits.before: Your W answers exactly one combo per fight — shield the spell that kills, not the one that stings.
edits.after: Past the river he has two blinks of escape and you have none — that shove is only worth a plate.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Standing still to detonate at half HP is one Riftwalk and a Nether Blade reset from dead — throw the E behind you and walk.

notes: The brief's derived flag marks Null Sphere as 'channel: interruptible', and missingInteractions claims Light Binding cancels it. Riot's own text says the opposite direction — Null Sphere 'interrupts channels', it is not itself a channel. Per the kit rule I trusted the description and wrote nothing claiming Lux's Q cancels his Q. Ratings on phases[0..4] were left untouched: I moved only the side and the why, since the rating scale's meaning on Lux-favoured rows was not decidable from the data. win[N] needed no edits — the content layer was already correct on all seven rows and the full layer was the one out of step.
